title: Stabilize lane-based admission and prewarm coordination to prevent cascading GPU queue amplification
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-14 a hosted API capacity event caused sustained GPU pool exhaustion for ~45 minutes, resulting in large request queue buildup, increased tail latencies, and widespread throttling for multiple tenants. This ticket captures the post-incident follow-ups to eliminate the root causes and harden admission/scaling paths to prevent similar cascading queue amplification in future surges.

What happened (brief): A traffic spike combined with a race in the prewarm/prefetch subsystem allowed prewarm jobs to consume admission credits and KV cache priming slots without being correctly classified as background work. The lane-based admission controller then mis-scored incoming requests under hysteresis conditions, admitting many low-effort prewarm tasks while blocking hot user requests. Autoscaler hysteresis combined with our current queue-growth heuristics delayed scale-up by ~3 minutes. The outcome was a feedback loop: growing queued requests triggered more prefetch attempts, which further starved GPU slots and prevented meaningful drain.

Why this matters: This class of failure impacts SLOs (p95/p99 latency), increases cost (wasted prewarm GPU cycles), and erodes tenant trust. The incident exposed gaps across admission scoring, prewarm isolation, autoscaler dynamics, and observability.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-02-14 12:03 UTC: First alert — queue depth on pool gpu-us-west-2 hit 80% of soft cap.
- 12:06 UTC: Initial autoscaler attempt started but suppressed by hysteresis window.
- 12:07 UTC: Spikes in prewarm job creation observed from prefix cache warmers for top-10 tenants.
- 12:12 UTC: Throttles applied broadly; manual emergency throttle of prewarm jobs enabled by on-call.
- 12:30 UTC: Manual priming and priority reweighting reduced ingress of background tasks.
- 12:48 UTC: Pool drained to steady state; mitigation actions left in monitoring.

Root cause analysis (concise):
1) Admission-scoring bug: prewarm/prefetch tasks were counted with the same admission weight as foreground requests under certain lane handoffs (race when lane metadata returned null).
2) No circuit-breaker for prewarm/foreground throttling: prewarm could consume a large portion of admission credits during surges.
3) Autoscaler heuristics: hysteresis and scale-up triggers ignored rapid queue growth rates; decision window too wide for steep spikes and did not consider prewarm fraction.
4) Observability gap: missing fine-grained metrics for prewarm vs. foreground GPU usage and KV-priming occupancy, making diagnosis slower.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident (already applied):
- Emergency flag to pause all prewarm jobs for 30m in affected pools (manual on-call action).
- Manual tenant-level priority override for Top 20 paying tenants to bypass prewarm lane.
- Temporary reduction of prewarm concurrency from 40 -> 8 across pools.
- Expanded alert thresholds for queue-growth rate in the monitoring dashboard.

Action items (owners, est, due):
- "Fix admission path to correctly classify prewarm/prefetch tasks when lane metadata is absent; add explicit lane tag fallback. Owner: Aditi Rao. Estimate: 5. Due: 2026-03-10." ,
- "Add a soft circuit-breaker that caps prewarm admission credits per pool and per tenant; circuit open if prewarm share > 20% for 60s. Owner: Daniel Park. Estimate: 5. Due: 2026-03-17." ,
- "Autoscaler: introduce 'queue-growth-rate' signal and a fast-scale policy that overrides hysteresis when growth > X reqs/s for > 30s. Owner: Priya Nair. Estimate: 8. Due: 2026-03-24." ,
- "Implement tenant-level concurrent prewarm caps and backoff strategy to prevent fanout storms. Owner: Miguel Torres. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-03." ,
- "Observability: add metrics (prewarm_gpu_seconds, foreground_gpu_seconds, kv_priming_slots_in_use) and dashboard panels; include alert playbook for combined metric patterns. Owner: Lina Chen. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-03." ,
- "Runbook updates: update hosted GPU exhaustion runbook to include prewarm pause, tenant priority override, and autoscaler fast-scale steps. Owner: SRE Team (owner: Omar Patel). Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-05." ,
- "Chaos test: create a synthetic test that simulates a 3x traffic spike with prewarm running to validate coupling protections. Owner: QE (owner: Hannah Lee). Estimate: 5. Due: 2026-03-17." ,
- "Post-deploy QA: smoke test for lane metadata null-handling + end-to-end stress test against staging GPU pool. Owner: Aditi Rao. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-18."

Acceptance criteria (what good looks like):
- Prewarm tasks are never admitted with full foreground weight when lane metadata is missing; unit + integration tests demonstrate correct classification.
- New circuit-breaker prevents prewarm from consuming >20% of admission credits in >95% of surge simulations.
- Autoscaler fast-scale triggers within 30s of high queue-growth bursts in 90% of synthetic tests.
- Dashboards surface prewarm vs foreground GPU consumption and alert within 60s of anomalous prewarm share.

Links and artifacts:
- Postmortem doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INC-2026-02-14-gpu-exhaustion
- Incident dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted/gpu-pool-exhaustion
- Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/15802 (admission-fix-wip)
- Emergency ops log (slack export): https://drive.google.com/opslog/driveid-incident-2026-02-14

Notes and rationale for prioritization:
- We prioritize admission classification and prewarm caps first because they are the lowest-effort, highest-impact changes that break the feedback loop. Autoscaler tuning is medium effort but depends on reliable signals (hence observability changes first).

Risks and open questions:
- Risk: aggressive prewarm caps could increase cold-start latency for low-latency tenants; need SLO tradeoffs documented per-tier.
- Open Q: Should prewarm be run in a completely separate maintenance pool for enterprise tenants? Cost/operational trade-offs to be explored in a follow-up design doc.

QA / verification plan:
- Merge admission fix behind feature-flag, run integration stress for 10k synthetic requests with active prewarm.
- Execute chaos test (planned above) on staging, measure p95/p99 and prewarm share.
- Gradual rollout to one region (us-west-2) with strict monitoring and rollback window.
